title: Microsurgical technique for cervical corpectomy and phrenic nerve access in the rat
author: Ghali
materials: All procedures were approved by the Drexel University Institutional Animal Care and Use Committee, which oversees Drexel University’s AAALAC International-accredited animal program. Spontaneously-breathing, Sprague-Dawley adult male rats (350–420 g) were anesthetized with isoflurane vaporized in O2 (Matrix; 4–5% induction, 2.0–2.5% maintenance) via a snout mask. The electrocardiogram (EKG) was measured via three small subcutaneous electrodes using conventional amplification and filtering (Neurolog; Digitimer, Hertfordshire, UK) and monitored using an audio amplifier (model AM10; Grass Instruments) and oscilloscope. Anesthetic depth was maintained at a level such that withdrawal reflexes and changes in heart rate in response to pinches of the distal hind limbs were absent. Following tracheotomy with an atraumatic glass tube, animals were artificially ventilated with the same gas mixture (45-65 cycles/min, 2.5–3.0 ml tidal volume; Columbus Apparatus). One femoral artery and vein were cannulated for measurement of arterial pressure and infusion of drugs/fluids, respectively. During initial surgical preparation and recordings, rectal temperature was maintained at 37.0 ± 0.1 °C via a servocontrolled heating blanket coupled to a rectal thermometer (Harvard Apparatus).

steps.title: Prepare animal and anesthesia
steps.instruction: Use adult male Sprague‑Dawley rats (350–420 g). Induce anesthesia with isoflurane vaporized in O₂ (Matrix) at 4–5 % for induction and maintain at 2.0–2.5 % via a snout mask. Monitor ECG with three sub‑cutaneous electrodes (Neurolog; Digitimer) amplified and filtered, audible via a Grass AM10 audio amp and displayed on an oscilloscope. Maintain anesthetic depth so that withdrawal reflexes and heart‑rate responses to hind‑limb pinches are absent.

steps.title: Perform tracheotomy and ventilation
steps.instruction: After tracheotomy, insert an atraumatic glass tube and connect to a ventilator delivering the same O₂‑isoflurane mixture at 45–65 breaths /min with a tidal volume of 2.5–3.0 ml (Columbus Apparatus).

steps.title: Cannulate femoral vessels and monitor temperature
steps.instruction: Cannulate one femoral artery for arterial pressure measurement and one femoral vein for drug/fluid infusion. Maintain rectal temperature at 37.0 ± 0.1 °C using a servocontrolled heating blanket linked to a Harvard Apparatus rectal thermometer.

steps.title: Make cervical incision and expose neck
steps.instruction: Make a midline cervical incision from the manubrium sterni to the level of the hyoid.

steps.title: Remove lymphoid tissue and submandibular gland
steps.instruction: Excise cervical lymphoid tissue together with the submandibular gland.

steps.title: Dissect sternocleidomastoid and sternohyoid
steps.instruction: Dissect the medial origin of the sternocleidomastoid from the sternum and medial clavicle and remove it to its mastoid insertion. Dissect the sternohyoid from its lateral origin, reflect it medially (or remove it entirely).

steps.title: Expose distal phrenic nerve
steps.instruction: Dissect soft tissue along the lymphatic duct to reveal the distal phrenic nerve, then reflect the lymphatic duct laterally to keep the nerve visible.

steps.title: Ligate and divide transverse cervical artery
steps.instruction: Grasp the transverse cervical artery with fine tweezers at two points to compress it, creating stasis and promoting thrombus formation; then divide the vessel by tearing it apart with the tweezers.

steps.title: Transect and ligate distal phrenic nerve
steps.instruction: Optionally retract the scalene muscle medially for better exposure, then transect the phrenic nerve distally and dissect proximally toward its root. Ligate the distal end with a 6‑0 braided silk suture.

steps.title: Ligate external jugular vein
steps.instruction: Identify the anterior branch of the external jugular vein, double‑ligate it using 4‑0 braided silk suture, and remove the vein.

steps.title: Ligate trachea and esophagus
steps.instruction: Securely ligate the trachea and esophagus together distally, then proximally, leaving two long free suture ends.

steps.title: Prepare for bundle evisceration
steps.instruction: Insert forceps through the oropharyngeal cavity into the esophagus and force them through the posterior esophageal wall. Grasp the two free suture ends with a needle holder.

steps.title: Eviscerate tracheo‑laryngo‑esophageo‑pharyngeal bundle
steps.instruction: Pull the tracheo‑laryngo‑esophageo‑pharyngeal bundle out through the oropharyngeal cavity, exposing the ventral musculature overlying the cervical vertebral column.

steps.title: Remove longus capiti and longus coli
steps.instruction: Excise the longus capiti muscles to reveal the longus coli; then remove the longus coli to expose the ventral surface of the cervical vertebral column.

steps.title: Perform cervical corpectomy
steps.instruction: Using a variable‑speed surgical drill, perform a corpectomy of the vascular vertebral bodies. Set the drill to a high speed to promote hemostasis by driving bone fragments into marrow channels. Pause frequently and irrigate continuously with saline to prevent overheating of bone and the ventral spinal cord surface.

steps.title: Open dura and protect spinal cord
steps.instruction: Open the dura in the midline and reflect it laterally. Irrigate the exposed spinal cord with artificial CSF and protect it with cottonoids soaked in the same solution.

steps.title: Apply filter pledget (optional)
steps.instruction: Place a filter‑paper pledget over the ventral surface of the spinal cord to prevent tissue drying.
